summary.headline: Rubicon Q2 FY27 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR577 crore and operating EBITDA reached 25%, with full-year operating EBITDA guidance raised to 24%+.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR576-577 crore, up 40% YoY from INR412 crore and up from INR534 crore in Q1. Pre-R&D EBITDA margin was 35.8% and operating EBITDA was INR144 crore (about 25% margin), up 53% YoY. Reported PAT rose to INR90 crore from INR54 crore YoY and INR85 crore in Q1, which included a one-time INR3.6 crore insurance claim. Results now include the Arinna Lifesciences consolidation (INR19.4 crore revenue, immaterial EBITDA contribution), and the company acquired a New Jersey manufacturing facility, which lifted capital employed and pre-revenue assets.

segments.name: Specialty / differentiated products
segments.commentary: Specialty products contributed 36% of gross profit in Q2. Management attributed margin expansion partly to specialty mix and to legacy products gaining share.

segments.name: Arinna Lifesciences
segments.commentary: Consolidated from this quarter with INR19.4 crore revenue and immaterial EBITDA contribution. Management is prioritising revenue growth and beating IPM growth before focusing on margins; no margin guidance given.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 operating EBITDA guidance raised to 24%+ from the earlier 23%+ (previously 22-23%).
Sequential USD revenue growth was 5% in Q2 after a pause in Q1 from tactical measures; management expects strong visibility for coming quarters.
Working capital days expected to normalise to 125-130 days from 117 days.
Pithampur (Indore) expected to contribute revenue from FY28 onwards.
R&D spend guidance of INR500 crore for the 2026-2027 cycle (plus Q1 FY28) is on track; INR313 crore already spent over six quarters.
Management expects FY30 incremental revenue from FY27-base R&D of INR500 crore; FY27 base cited as INR2,105 crore (annualised H1 ex-Arinna).
capex_capacity: Four manufacturing sites: all inspected within the last six months. New Jersey (FDA inspected May 2026, EIR in place); Ambernath and Satara (unannounced inspections in October 2026); Pithampur (inspected July 2026, two observations, response filed, EIR awaited).

Ambernath inspection in October 2026 had three systems observations and two product-application observations; management says all are procedural with no data-integrity issues. Satara had one procedural observation, response submitted, EIR awaited.
Both R&D sites (Canada and Thane HQ) have EIRs in place with no observations.
Pre-revenue assets: Pithampur (operational soon), Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (CSN, no timeline given), New Jersey (no revenue date; requires filings, product transfer and FDA inspection).
New Jersey facility: fixed assets rose INR85 crore, cash payout INR29 crore, INR55 crore non-cash right-of-use.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth described as well-balanced across products; top 5 and top 10 product revenue ranges stable over four sequential quarters, with no hero product.
Pricing stable, supported by specialty and differentiated product focus.
Commercialisation rate 84%; three approvals received in Q2.
Licensing rule change in India: export licence can only be applied for after FDA approval, so some approved products will ship in the coming quarter rather than immediately.
R&D productivity (3-year incremental product sales per unit of prior R&D) rose to 5.8-5.9x for the 2024-27 cycle from 3.3x (2021-24) and 4.1x (2022-25).

qa_highlights.question: What share of R&D is wasted or does not convert to revenue, and will that change?
qa_highlights.answer: Sagar Oak said a stage-gated process with de-risking before major capital commitment keeps non-productive spend low. Some projects are paused or stopped late in their life cycle; no quantified waste figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rising R&D-to-revenue productivity from higher revenue per molecule or better efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination of both. Portfolio is moving toward drug-device combinations and larger individual opportunities, with no hero products.

qa_highlights.question: Why does slide 13 base revenue (INR839 crore for FY24) differ from audited figures (about INR854 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: The slide shows product sales only, excluding services; the Arinna numbers are also excluded.

qa_highlights.question: When will the three pre-revenue facilities start contributing revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pithampur from FY28 onwards. CSN has no timeline. New Jersey needs filings, product placement and FDA inspection first, so no date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Where could Arinna margins settle in the medium to long term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide. Focus is on restoring growth and beating IPM growth first; profitability is some way off.

qa_highlights.question: What is the drivers of margin expansion: low-margin product exits, specialty mix, or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination of share gains by legacy products, specialty mix in gross profit, and operating leverage, net of geopolitical-related cost pressures. Tactical product rationalisation measures are largely complete, with a few finishing in one or two quarters.

risks_watch: Regulatory: Ambernath (three systems and two application observations) and Satara and Pithampur EIRs are pending; outcomes will affect commercialisation.
Export licensing rule change may delay shipment of approved products into the next quarter.
Pre-revenue assets (about 25% of capital employed, ~INR400 crore) dilute ROACE until Pithampur, CSN and New Jersey start contributing; no date given for CSN or New Jersey.
Arinna is still loss-making or at best immaterial to EBITDA, with no margin guidance; it is in a growth-recovery phase.
Geopolitical cost pressures are cited as affecting gross margin; quantification not provided.
Working capital at 117 days is expected to revert to 125-130 days.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and margin delivery, and openly cautious on timelines: management declined to give dates for CSN and New Jersey and gave no Arinna margin guidance. Answers on R&D waste were qualitative, and the Ambernath inspection outcome was framed as procedural and still pending.
key_quotes: If you look at all the parameters, revenue, EBITDA, and PAT, we've had a strong performance.
We are happy to report that now we are guiding it to 24% plus for the full year.
First, again, the focus, as Nitin said, would be on revenue and then on margins.
All the three sites are not contributing anything in revenue right now.

growth.why: Operating EBITDA margin guidance raised to 24%+ for FY27 (from 23%+) with no explicit revenue growth guidance; support cited is sequential USD growth of 5%, stable pricing, specialty mix and 84% commercialisation, with new capacity (Pithampur) not contributing until FY28 and no utilisation figure given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 operating EBITDA margin guidance raised to 24%+ from 23%+, with Q2 operating EBITDA at about 25% (INR144 crore) versus INR94 crore a year earlier, driven by specialty mix (36% of gross profit) and operating leverage, partly offset by geopolitical cost pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pithampur is expected to contribute revenue from FY28 onwards and is described as operational soon, but CSN has no timeline and New Jersey has no revenue date, so only one facility has a date.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Sequential USD revenue grew 5% in Q2 after a Q1 pause, and management expects strong visibility, but no explicit revenue growth guidance was given and H1 revenue rose 45% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Operating EBITDA guidance was already raised to 24%+ from 23%+ and Q2 margin came in at about 25%, while management cites strong visibility; no revenue guidance was given to upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ambernath (three systems and two application observations) and Satara and Pithampur EIRs are pending, export licence rules may delay shipments, and working capital is expected to rise from 117 days to 125-130 days.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Commercialisation rate is 84% with three approvals in Q2, and some approved products will ship next quarter after export licence filing, though no specific product names were given.

rows.label: Ambernath and Satara EIRs pending
rows.why: Ambernath had three systems and two product-application observations and Satara had one procedural observation, with responses filed and EIRs awaited; management calls them procedural but outcomes will gate commercialisation.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation to 125-130 days
rows.why: Net working capital days were 117 versus 126 a year earlier, and management expects them to revert to 125-130 days, which would absorb cash.

rows.label: Arinna Lifesciences margin recovery
rows.why: Arinna contributed INR19.4 crore revenue with immaterial EBITDA, management declined to guide margins and is prioritising growth, so profitability is some way off.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth and the raised 24%+ EBITDA margin guide, but cautious on timelines for CSN and New Jersey and gave no Arinna margin guidance; analysts pressed on R&D waste and the drivers of margin expansion, and got qualitative answers.
